articles.title: Ina Garten's Chive Biscuits Recipe for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: A novice baker attempted Ina Garten's tried-and-true recipe for chive biscuits from scratch, finding the process surprisingly easy.
articles.content: A novice baker's quest for the perfect Thanksgiving biscuits led me to Ina Garten's tried-and-true recipe. With her guidance, I attempted to make chive biscuits from scratch, a task that seemed daunting but ultimately proved surprisingly easy. Garten's recipe is remarkably straightforward and requires minimal ingredients, which made it an attractive choice for a beginner like myself. A batch of eight chive biscuits can be made with just 2 cups of all-purpose flour, half-and-half, cold unsalted butter, baking powder, kosher salt, sugar, egg, and chopped fresh chives or parsley. The recipe's brevity was a welcome respite from more complex baking tasks, and I found the process to be remarkably quick. Preheating the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit set the stage for mixing the dry ingredients first, which included flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar. Garten's chive biscuits are renowned for their buttery, light, and fluffy texture, qualities that seemed like a tall order for a novice baker. With a limited number of ingredients and steps involved, I was eager to see if her recipe would deliver on its promise of ease and quality. As I began preparing the dough, I couldn't help but think about Garten's reputation as the go-to chef for Thanksgiving cooking. Her recipes are often cited as perfect for special occasions, and it seemed like making chive biscuits from scratch using her recipe was a great way to put that claim to the test. I added the dry ingredients - flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar - to the bowl of my electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. This initial step was straightforward, requiring minimal effort on my part. The dry ingredients were simply poured into the mixing bowl and left to await further processing. With all the dry components in place, I felt a sense of anticipation for what was to come. Next, I added the diced butter to the mixing bowl. As I began to mix on low speed, the butter started to break down and combine with the dry ingredients. The mixture began to resemble coarse crumbs, a sign that the butter was starting to integrate into the dough. With the mixer still on low, I added the half-and-half, watching as it incorporated smoothly into the mixture. The mixture needed only a brief stirring to ensure everything was just combined, according to Garten's instructions. This gentle approach helped maintain the delicate balance of ingredients and prevented over-working the dough. After this initial mixing step, I added the chopped chives, introducing their fresh flavor and aroma into the mix. With the addition of the chives, the mixture still needed some further processing. In line with Garten's advice to beat the mixture until it's just combined, I continued to mix for a short while longer. This brief kneading process helped bring the dough together, creating a cohesive mass that was ready in mere minutes. The ease and speed of this initial mixing and kneading surprised me, given my limited experience with making dough from scratch. Kneading is an essential step in developing the gluten that gives biscuits their structure and softness. I used the heels of my hands to push down on the dough and then push it outward as I kneaded. The process involves folding the dough in half towards myself and pushing it down and out again with the heels of my hands. To ensure the dough didn't become too sticky, I made sure to add flour whenever necessary during the kneading process. This helped me maintain a consistent texture throughout the dough. As I repeated the steps, I tried to knead the dough into a rectangle shape as instructed by Garten. While attempting to achieve a ¾-inch thickness, my kneading was somewhat uneven, resulting in some biscuits being slightly thinner than others. However, keeping the dough on the thicker side is recommended for fluffier biscuits. This is an important consideration when shaping the biscuits before baking. Once I had shaped all the biscuits, I moved on to preparing the egg wash. Mixing one egg with one tablespoon of water created a ready-to-use mixture that helped give the biscuits their golden-brown color. The egg wash was applied evenly to each biscuit before they were placed in the preheated oven. Before throwing the pan into the oven, I made sure to brush each biscuit with the egg wash, which plays a crucial role in achieving the desired color and texture of the biscuits. The biscuits were done to perfection in just 22 minutes, following Ina Garten's recommended baking time. Garten advises that the biscuits are ready when their tops are golden brown and the insides are firm, a clear indicator of their doneness. The chive biscuits turned out beautifully, with a lovely golden hue and a satisfying crunch on top that gave way to a buttery and fluffy interior. The combination of saltiness from the ingredients and the pop of color from the chives made for a delightful flavor experience. Despite these positive developments, the team's overall record remains a major concern, with a disappointing 2-7 start to the season. It appears that not just one or two areas are in need of improvement, but rather the entire roster is struggling to find its footing. The Eagles will be looking to regroup during their upcoming bye week. In other encouraging news for the team, punter Braden Mann has been a bright spot, showcasing his exceptional leg with an impressive 86-yard punt against the Giants. This effort not only highlights his individual talent but also underscores the importance of special teams in contributing to the team's overall success. The Philadelphia Eagles' roster has seen a decline in performance this season, except for one notable exception - DeVonta Smith's teammate, who managed to shine despite his teammates struggling. Meanwhile, linebacker Zack Baun suffered a back injury during the game after being hit, forcing coach Matt McCarthy out of the action temporarily. Notably, Baun had an impressive outing with two sacks, marking the most he has achieved in one game since his debut in the 2024 season opener. articles.title: Observations of Social Interactions Among Wild Assamese Macaques Reveal Benefits for Group Hierarchy Position
articles.summary: Researchers observed 46 male Assamese macaques in Thailand over two years and found that watching friendly interactions can lead to stronger social bonds and higher ranks.
articles.content: Observations of social interactions among wild Assamese macaques have revealed that watching others can be beneficial for an individual's position within the group hierarchy. Researchers from Germany's DPZ and the University of Göttingen conducted a two-year study in Thailand, focusing on 46 male Assamese macaques. The team observed how long these animals spent observing other males interacting with each other during social encounters. The scientists recorded more than 440 instances where a macaque watched two other males engage in interactions, which were categorized as either friendly or aggressive. These observations suggest that the ability to observe and evaluate social interactions may be an essential skill for macaques. By studying how these animals allocate their attention towards others, researchers hope to gain insights into the evolution of social intelligence in primates. Males that spent more time watching friendly interactions within their group developed closer social bonds with specific other males by the end of the first year. These stronger bonds led to higher ranks in the dominance hierarchy for these males by the second year, a significant finding that highlights the importance of social connections in primate societies. The research suggests that observing others is not just about learning new behaviors or gaining knowledge, but also about building relationships and alliances that ultimately contribute to social success. This understanding can be seen as a crucial step in deciphering the evolution of social intelligence in primates. In fact, the data show that males who interfered more frequently in social situations had likely gained valuable information from their observations, which helped them decide when and how to intervene. The researchers found that observing aggressive interactions did not have a direct impact on social bonding or dominance success among males. In fact, the amount of time they spent watching fights had no bearing on their position in the group hierarchy. A different explanation seems to be at play when it comes to managing risk during conflicts. All males appeared to watch closely during fights, as none wanted to get drawn into a dispute against their will. This uniform behavior did not give any individual an advantage over others. The study's findings suggest that observing others is linked to forming closer social bonds. These stronger relationships in turn lead to higher dominance ranks and greater mating success. According to the researchers, this sequence of events implies a causal relationship between observation and bonding. Studies like this one help shed light on how social intelligence has evolved over time. Humans also tend to keep track of who gets along with whom and who is arguing. If observing others provides an advantage in other primates, it could offer clues about why this ability developed in our primate relatives, and potentially even in humans. The researchers propose that observing others may have become a crucial skill for survival in social groups, ultimately contributing to the evolution of advanced social intelligence. Observing others' interactions within a group may have played a crucial role in the evolution of advanced social intelligence among primates. This idea is supported by research showing that male macaques who pay attention to their peers' behavior are more likely to achieve higher ranks and secure mating opportunities. articles.title: Feline Chronic Kidney Disease Diagnosis Breakthrough
articles.summary: Researchers have made significant progress in identifying potential biomarkers that could help diagnose and treat chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats.
articles.content: A Breakthrough in Diagnosing Feline Chronic Kidney Disease Researchers have made significant progress in identifying potential biomarkers that could help diagnose and treat chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats. This debilitating condition often goes undiagnosed until its late stages, making it difficult to manage effectively. A recent study published in the Journal of Proteome Research has shed new light on how feline CKD develops, offering veterinarians valuable insights into detecting different stages of the disease. Feline chronic kidney disease is a broad term that encompasses various disorders causing kidney damage and dysfunction. The condition is particularly prevalent among older cats, making it challenging to distinguish between natural aging and disease progression. In some cases, definitive diagnoses may require invasive procedures such as biopsies and extensive laboratory tests, which can be time-consuming and costly. The study's findings are promising for cat owners and veterinarians alike. While blood-based biomarkers do exist, they often fail to pinpoint the root cause of kidney dysfunction or only detect mid-to-late stages of feline CKD. The newly identified protein biomarkers in urine could help fill this diagnostic gap, enabling veterinarians to develop more targeted treatments. The discovery of these potential biomarkers is a significant step towards improving feline health care. Further research will be necessary to validate their effectiveness and explore their potential as diagnostic tools. For now, the study's findings offer hope for cat owners struggling with the challenges of managing this irreversible condition. The search for more precise biomarkers is a pressing issue in the medical community, not just limited to feline chronic kidney disease (CKD). According to lead researcher Katelyn Brusach, this challenge is common across various chronic diseases. To address this problem, Brusach and her team conducted a study using urine as a non-invasive sample to further characterize CKD. The research analyzed urine from 30 healthy cats and 34 cats with CKD, identifying over 2,000 proteins in feline urine. One protein, MMP-7, showed promise as an early-stage biomarker for CKD, with higher levels detected in patients than in healthy controls. However, a single biomarker may not provide a comprehensive understanding of the disease. Chronic diseases are often complex and heterogeneous, making it difficult to encapsulate them with a single protein. Brusach noted that this is why her team sought to utilize urinary protein profiles to measure how different protein groups trend across the disease. The researchers found three distinct subgroups of proteins in the urine samples from cats with late-stage CKD. These subgroups could potentially be used to classify different types of the disease and inform treatment plans, providing a more nuanced understanding of the condition. Researchers have made significant progress in identifying new biomarkers for diagnosing feline chronic kidney disease (CKD). By analyzing a comprehensive list of proteins present in cat urine, they were able to pinpoint distinct patterns that could distinguish between different stages of the disease. These protein profiles may provide a more accurate and nuanced understanding of CKD in cats than traditional markers, which can sometimes miss subtle changes. This breakthrough has the potential to revolutionize the way veterinarians diagnose and treat feline kidney disease, allowing for more targeted treatment plans. The discovery paves the way for further research into the development of clinical biomarkers for feline CKD diagnosis and treatment, ultimately leading to improved health outcomes for cats affected by this condition. articles.content: Martine Rose has been named as Balenciaga's new creative director, marking a historic moment for the French fashion house and cementing her status as a leading figure in menswear. This appointment comes after months of speculation and rumors, which have finally been confirmed with the announcement that Rose will be taking over from Pierpaolo Piccioli, who is leaving Balenciaga after just three seasons at the helm. The British-Jamaican designer has spent nearly two decades building a reputation for her eponymous label, which has gained an outsize influence in the fashion world through its unique visual language and collaborations with streetwear brands. Rose's clothes are characterized by their playful styling, graphic-driven sportswear, offbeat tailoring, and covetable sneaker collaborations, often incorporating unconventional elements such as lace-up fastenings on soccer jerseys or chap-covered suit trousers. Rose's approach to fashion challenges traditional notions of style, often blending sportswear and tailoring in unexpected ways. On her runways, these two seemingly disparate elements frequently share center stage, reflecting her willingness to defy conventions. Her design aesthetic draws inspiration from London's rich subcultural heritage, incorporating influences from rave culture, football fandom, and mod styles. This eclecticism is a hallmark of Rose's approach, with no emphasis on creating outfits that conform to traditional notions of style. Martine Rose's influence extends far beyond the runway. Her designs have been worn by some of the most recognizable figures in entertainment, including Drake, Timothée Chalamet, Bad Bunny, and A$AP Rocky. One notable example of her high-profile styling is Kendrick Lamar's 2025 Super Bowl halftime performance. He wore a custom red, white, and blue leather varsity jacket designed by Rose, an outfit that undoubtedly added to the spectacle of the event. Rose has managed to transcend fashion's tribal boundaries, earning coverage from both mainstream publications like Vogue and online fashion hubs such as Hypebeast. Her appearances at London Fashion Week have become a staple, and she made her Milan debut in 2024. In addition to her runway presence, Rose has collaborated with several prominent brands, including Supreme, for whom she has produced two highly successful collections. She has also worked with Nike to reimagine the Shox and Monarch sneakers, turning them into coveted items among sneaker enthusiasts. Martine Rose's appointment as creative director at Balenciaga marks a significant shift in her career trajectory. She has spent years building an idiosyncratic brand that blends high-end fashion with streetwear sensibilities. Rose's ability to reimagine familiar clothes and make them feel fresh is one of the key reasons she was hired by Kering, the luxury group that owns Balenciaga. Her talent lies in taking existing styles and turning them into something unexpected and desirable. As she takes on this new challenge, Rose will have access to vast resources and a global platform, presenting her with both opportunities and constraints. articles.summary: Lawmakers have arrived on Capitol Hill for a brief lame-duck session following last week's midterm elections, which saw significant gains for Democrats that will redefine the balance of power in Washington come January.
articles.content: Lawmakers have arrived on Capitol Hill for a brief lame-duck session following last week's midterm elections, which saw significant gains for Democrats that will redefine the balance of power in Washington come January. As their majorities dwindle, Republicans are scrambling to maximize their influence during this final stretch before the new year. Their efforts aim to leave a lasting impact despite their losses. Key priorities include selecting new leaders and averting potential government shutdowns. With these pressing concerns, Republican lawmakers will focus on navigating the remaining days of their majority. Leadership elections have begun with House Republicans set to hold their vote on Tuesday, while House Democrats will convene in the following week and Senate Democrats in early December. The Senate Republican leadership elections are scheduled for this Tuesday morning, but some members are pushing for a delay in light of last week's midterm losses. Led by Senator Ron Johnson from Wisconsin, at least a handful of senators want to reassess their approach before proceeding with the elections. Johnson has written a letter to his colleagues arguing that holding leadership elections without discussing and evaluating the candidates' leadership plans would be irresponsible. He claims that the letter will be signed by at least five of his fellow senators, as required by Senate rules. Senate leaders are grappling with the aftermath of their party's midterm losses, acknowledging that a thorough examination of what went wrong is necessary. Leadership elections for Senate Democrats are scheduled to take place early next month, as they prepare to navigate the challenges ahead. Government funding remains a pressing concern, with a deadline looming on December 11. This will force lawmakers to work under intense pressure to pass the 12 annual appropriations bills required to fund the federal government. The initial deadline of September 30 was extended when Congress approved a short-term measure earlier this year, avoiding a potentially messy funding fight ahead of the midterm elections. As lawmakers return to Capitol Hill for their final stretch of work before the new year, they face a packed agenda and mounting pressure from within their own party. The war in Iran is likely to be a contentious issue, with some Democrats looking to use their leverage to block funding for the conflict, which has been met with widespread disapproval among voters. This move could have far-reaching consequences, including a potential government shutdown that would carry over into the new Congress and distract from other pressing priorities. Meanwhile, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's leadership is under intense scrutiny following the Republican Party's significant losses in the midterm elections. Critics argue that his strategy on Iran has been unclear and ineffective, sparking calls for his impeachment or resignation. Congress also faces a looming deadline to pass its annual defense policy bill, which could be complicated by opposition to the Iran war and ongoing concerns about Hegseth's leadership of the Pentagon. As Congress returns from its break, the focus is shifting to contentious legislation and leadership challenges within the Republican Party. In an unusual statement, Rep. Massie hinted that he might reconsider introducing articles of impeachment against Pentagon Secretary Hegseth if he were to resign. However, other Republicans remain noncommittal about supporting the impeachment effort, with some lawmakers taking a cautious approach. For instance, Rep. French Hill of Arkansas has not explicitly stated his stance on the issue. His silence reflects the delicate balance of power within the party. The House's push for a third reconciliation bill is also facing obstacles in the Senate, where time is running out to pass key legislation. The upper chamber will return this week with a packed schedule, including confirmation hearings and votes on President Trump's administration and judicial nominees. As Congress returns from its midterm elections break, Republicans remain committed to their legislative agenda despite significant losses for the party. In a defiant tone, Pete Hegseth expressed his party's resolve in a social media video, stating "We don't back down" and implying that they will continue to push forward with their priorities. The upper chamber's packed schedule this week includes confirmation hearings and votes on key nominees, while also leaving room for potential reconciliation packages. However, such efforts could jeopardize bipartisan negotiations over appropriations bills, according to Representative Rosa DeLauro. Meanwhile, Senator John Thune had previously expressed openness to a third reconciliation bill but acknowledged the need for 50 votes, which he admitted was lacking at the time of his statement in late October. articles.title: OnePlus Smartwatches Offer Impressive Battery Life but Lack Certain Features
articles.summary: The OnePlus Watch 4 boasts an impressive five days of use on a single charge, while also offering up to two weeks when using power saver mode.
articles.content: OnePlus smartwatches have long been known for their impressive battery life, offering an unbeatable combination of performance and value. However, when compared to rival devices, they often fall short on certain features that enthusiasts crave. The niche appeal of OnePlus devices has always set them apart from more mainstream brands. While the company's phones have garnered a loyal following, its smartwatches have struggled to gain widespread recognition in the market. Despite the uncertainty surrounding OnePlus' future plans for its US and European markets, there are still options available for those interested in purchasing one of these devices. The official OnePlus store is currently unable to sell new smartwatches in the US, but online retailers like Amazon continue to stock a wide range of models. One notable advantage that OnePlus smartwatches have over their competitors is battery life. The Watch 4, for instance, boasts an impressive five days of use on a single charge when running in smart mode and up to two weeks when using power saver mode. The question remains: what benefits do you gain by choosing an OnePlus smartwatch over other brands? Will the potential savings and superior performance be enough to make up for any missing features, or are there better alternatives available in the market? OnePlus smartwatches have a significant advantage when it comes to charging speed. In performance tests, a OnePlus Watch 3 was able to reach up to 80% charge in just 30 minutes. This is impressive compared to other popular smartwatch models, such as the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra, which reached only 50% and 36% respectively in the same time frame. The rapid charging capabilities of OnePlus watches are a major plus for users who need their devices to be constantly available. With an OnePlus watch, there's little risk of running out of battery even with heavy usage. The speedy charging is likely due to the advanced technology used by OnePlus, which allows for efficient energy transfer and storage. Another significant advantage of OnePlus smartwatches is their affordability without sacrificing quality. Despite being priced lower than comparable competitors, OnePlus watches offer large, bright AMOLED screens and solid build quality. This makes them an attractive option for users who want a high-quality smartwatch without breaking the bank. The onboard software, known as OHealth, on OnePlus watches is serviceable but not exceptional. However, users can still access a full suite of Google apps, which makes up for any shortcomings in the native software. The availability of Google apps ensures that users have access to all the features and functionality they need from their smartwatch. OnePlus watches are also notable for their build quality, which is solid and durable. This is particularly important for devices intended for use during physical activity, where a reliable and rugged design can make a big difference. The traditional watch-like design of OnePlus watches is also aesthetically pleasing to some users, although this may not be the case for everyone. The lack of cellular support on OnePlus watches is a significant drawback, as it limits their functionality without pairing with a phone. Additionally, US models are missing ECG trackers due to regulatory issues, and older OnePlus Watch 2 models also lack fall detection. These omissions mean that some users may find the features they need in competing smartwatch models. OnePlus smartwatches are not for everyone due to their chunky design, which may be a drawback for those who prefer sleeker timepieces. Their size can also make them difficult to wear on slimmer wrists, and they weigh more than some competing models, potentially causing discomfort over extended periods of use. The company has pledged to provide software updates for existing devices, but it remains uncertain how accessible this support will be. This concern may be more pressing for smartphone users who rely heavily on software updates, although smartwatch owners tend to require fewer updates overall. articles.title: Chalmers University of Technology Aalto University Aalborg University
articles.summary: A recent study has highlighted varying views among teachers regarding what students should learn and how interdisciplinarity should be implemented in the classroom.
articles.content: A growing trend in education is incorporating interdisciplinarity into curricula, where students learn from multiple fields of study to tackle complex problems. This approach is particularly relevant for engineering students, who are often tasked with working on projects that require knowledge from various disciplines. However, a recent study has highlighted the varying views among teachers regarding what students should learn and how interdisciplinarity should be implemented in the classroom. Researchers conducted interviews with 18 educators from three universities: Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden, Aalto University in Finland, and Aalborg University in Denmark. The study revealed that some teachers focus on bringing together students from different disciplinary backgrounds to foster collaboration and teamwork. This approach emphasizes forming diverse student groups with a range of expertise to tackle complex projects. In contrast, other educators prioritize the integration of knowledge, theories, and methods from various disciplines, focusing on which perspectives students need to draw upon. This dichotomy in teaching approaches raises questions about what interdisciplinarity truly means in an educational context. While some teachers see it as a way to promote collaboration and diversity, others view it as an opportunity to integrate different bodies of knowledge and expertise. As the study demonstrates, the implementation of interdisciplinarity varies significantly among educators, reflecting differing views on its core principles and goals. The researchers' findings highlight the need for further discussion and clarification on what students should learn when engaging with interdisciplinary projects. The concept of interdisciplinarity in engineering education is often borrowed from other disciplines without considering how it applies specifically to this field. To address this issue, researchers developed a model consisting of four dimensions for understanding interdisciplinary education. These dimensions are not mutually exclusive and can overlap or be combined within the same course, allowing teachers to tailor their approach. The model aims to provide a framework for teaching teams to clarify expectations and make informed decisions about curriculum development. By using this tool, instructors can ensure that students gain specific skills from joint projects, such as learning to coordinate work or develop shared methods of problem-solving. Disciplinary dynamics also play a significant role in interdisciplinary collaborations. Research has shown that engineering and natural sciences tend to dominate these interactions, often relegating the humanities and social sciences to secondary roles. This imbalance raises questions about how students from different disciplines can effectively collaborate on joint projects. To effectively teach interdisciplinarity, teachers must consider which perspectives are given space and who gets to define the problem. This requires them to reflect on their own biases and assumptions. Teachers planning interdisciplinary lessons need to strike a balance between different viewpoints, ensuring that students from various disciplines can collaborate successfully. articles.title: Giant Stone Axes in Britain May Have Been Crafted for Show
articles.summary: A new study on prehistoric stone axes suggests that some of these massive handaxes were created as status symbols, rather than practical tools.
articles.content: Giant stone axes discovered in Britain may have been crafted more for show than for use as tools. These massive handaxes, some measuring up to 285 millimeters long, date back over 300,000 years to a time when hominins inhabited the region. The creation of these enormous tools required great skill and effort, but their design makes them impractical for everyday use. Weighing up to three kilograms and reaching lengths of up to 30 centimeters, they would have been fragile and difficult to wield. According to Malaika Standley Barrow at University College London, the primary purpose of these giant handaxes may not have been for chopping or cutting, but rather as a status symbol. These prehistoric artifacts were likely crafted to impress others within their group. Ficrons are a type of Stone Age handaxe characterized by curved sides, rounded bases, and sharp pointed tips. They have appeared in British archaeological records since the late 19th century, particularly along the Thames River and its tributaries. The discovery of giant stone axes in British archaeological records has raised questions about their purpose and significance. While most handaxes from this period are relatively small, measuring between 8 to 15 centimetres in length, a few exceptional examples exceed two or even three times the usual size. Researchers led by Standley Barrow examined 817 handaxes from seven sites across southern Britain, including the Thames valley, Kent, Hampshire, and Devon. Among these tools were seven giant axes measuring at least 22 centimetres long, which were found to have distinct characteristics that set them apart from smaller versions. 3D scans and measurements revealed that six of the seven giant handaxes had exaggerated proportions compared to smaller axes from the same sites. The larger axes also tended to be more symmetrical and have straighter edges, suggesting they were crafted with greater skill and precision than their smaller counterparts. This suggests that the giant handaxes were not simply scaled-up versions of standard tools but rather deliberately crafted to stand out visually, according to Standley Barrow. The researchers behind the study decided to test the performance of these massive stone axes by creating replicas and having students use them to cut through rope. To do this, they commissioned 10 giant and 10 normal-sized replica flint knives from experienced knappers, who worked with British flint to create the tools. These replicas were then used by 20 students in a series of experiments, where each student first tried cutting through a piece of rope attached to a metal frame using a standard-sized knife, followed by attempting to cut it with the giant version. The results showed that while making the giant knives was much more time-consuming for the knappers - taking around 45 minutes on average compared to 20-30 minutes for smaller ones. The massive stone axes, known as ficrons, would have been impractical for everyday tasks like butchering or digging due to their weight and fragility, making them prone to breaking under pressure. However, researchers suggest that these enormous tools may have served a dual purpose - both ceremonial and practical. They could have been used to deliver the final blow to an already wounded animal, known as the coup de grâce, which would have required minimal force and pressure on the blade. The age of these artifacts indicates they were likely crafted by early Neanderthals, whose exquisite craftsmanship suggests a sophisticated appreciation for aesthetics and cultural tradition. This finding highlights the intelligence and social complexity of our ancient ancestors, who used technology to survive and interact with each other in recognizable ways.
